dossier.public_summary: The signal is not consistent: alternate dips are >10 times deeper than alternate ones and the depth jumps from near zero to many hundred ppm between sectors and between individual transits. This pattern matches an eclipsing binary or systematic noise, not a steady small planet the size of 1.3 Earth radii.

reasons.why: Even and odd dips differ by ~100% at 12.76 sigma, strongly favouring a binary at twice the 14.5 d period rather than a planet.
Depth changes dramatically between sectors and even within the same pipeline, from 2 and -73 ppm to 2203 ppm; a true planet should be steady.
reasons.value: p_constant 5.373e-38, depth_change_pct 343.9, sector_depths_by_source changes_within_a_source with p_constant 1.2645822388938858e-15 (SPOC 2-min) and 6.124585305594828e-26 (TESS-SPOC)

reasons.why: Individual transits are highly inconsistent; the nominal 411 ppm signal comes from a few recent deep outlying events, a hallmark of systematics or a blended/eclipsing binary rather than a planet.
